data.name: Park Bound
data.detailed_description:
Park Bound is a massively multiplayer playground featuring player crafted parks. Parks contain a variety of open worlds to explore and play with other players. Each world has different goals, obstacles, and collectible treasures used to unlock more challenging levels. Jump across traps, dodge obstacles, pick up jetpacks, soar through the sky with gliders, and even roll inside balls to complete objectives.

Features

  • Playable solo, with friends, and other players you find in the parks.
  • Explore and collect treasures in the main park created by the developer and parks created by the community.
  • Variety of levels types from platforming obstacle courses, party-style mini-games, to explorable sandboxes.
  • Pick up jetpacks, gliders, gyroballs, double jump, and more - each changing how you play the levels.
  • Includes in-game level editor where you can create your own network of worlds combined as a park.
  • Build and share your own objects or use existing libraries created by the developer and other players.

The Parks

The game is a continually growing ecosystem of parks created by both the community and the developer. Each park, managed by a single player, is its own self contained universe that offers consistent level quality as well as a place to return to as more levels are created. Parks can be visited by jumping into portals located throughout the hub world or by using the in-game park browser.


Each park is filled with levels that can be created with a variety of styles and objectives. Some levels may be an intense obstacle course requiring expert precision, analysis, and execution. Other levels may be open worlds with a variety of smaller challenges to be completed independently. Levels can have special rewards for taking difficult paths, finding secret locations, completing a section under a specified time limit, or gathering collectibles in a dangerous area.

Level Editor

As a creator, the level editor gives you full control of everything in your park. Once the park is opened it is always online and accessible to anyone with the game. You can watch your park from above, play alongside visitors, and view real-time population metrics to gather valuable feedback about your levels.


The level editor gives the tools to create spaces efficiently without limitations. Using a visual interface creators build entire levels without any programming or scripting languages. The editor provides customizable shape primitives, terrain, voxels, materials, animations, lighting, music, sound effects, particles, prefabs, and more. Prefabs give designers the ability to create complex re-usable objects in discrete packages. Park Bound embraces an open design philosophy where creations can be shared and modified freely between authors. This atmosphere of collaboration allows authors to combine and improve existing ideas to create new worlds.

reviews.review:
[h1]Overview:[/h1]
I happened to come across this game not too long ago and, having now played 400+ hours of it, I'm really glad I did. The gameplay is fun, the community is welcoming, the creation tools are flexible, and the developer (Bambastic Games) is friendly and attentive to the game and its players. That's the abridged review, so now for the details:

[h1]Quick Note for Parents:[/h1]
This online game allows all players to type chat messages to each other and create almost anything they want in their own levels. The developer can moderate content whenever possible, but the potential for inappropriate content to eventually surface will always be present in games of this nature. Fortunately, the community tries to stray away from producing questionable content. However, I still highly recommend adult supervision for younger gamers during online play in ANY game. Safety first!

[h1]Gameplay:[/h1]
If you've played 3D platformers before, you probably have a good idea of how the controls feel. The moveset is simple and your character's running and jumping movements are very precise, but not overly sensitive. There's also a variety of in-level items to enhance or change your movement options such as Double Jump, Jetpack, and a ball to roll around in. The collision detection is also very polished, especially considering it has to work with a variety of level designs. If other players are online, while you may see them playing and chatting with you in levels, their actions do not directly affect you.

The Parks in the game function as hub worlds. These hubs are created by players and can be used as gateways to the levels they make, much like Super Mario 64. Everyone is allowed to make only 1 hub world at the moment, but can add as many levels as they want to it. The main goal of each level is to reach its treasure chest, which has a fun little user-made treasure inside that can be viewed later in the hub. Stars can also be collected for completing certain level objectives. Your completion progress in all parks is automatically saved so you can continue where you left off upon revisiting them. Parks and individual levels can be searched for in the Park Browser, which can be found in the menu or the main lobby.

You can create a simple custom character with some neat options for hair and accessories. Each aspect of the character can be recolored as you please. You can also change your appearance at any time from the changing room in the main starting hub, which is nice. The hub also has the occasional special challenge that allows you to nab a snazzy new accessory if you complete it within a certain timeframe.

[h1]Editor:[/h1]
Where to even begin? If you look to the left of the house in the main lobby, you'll see a teleporter with a sign that says "BUILD", which takes you to the level editor. This is where I spend much of my play time, which is for a good reason. There are so many options that I've had almost no trouble getting my raw level ideas into motion. All it requires is a little time.

If you prefer a simple level-editing experience, you can choose from an extensive list of pre-made objects to drag and drop into your levels. If you're a bit more daring, you can switch to Advanced Mode (my preferred way to build), create primitive shapes, assign behaviors and modifiers to them, and set their materials/color. You can even turn groups of connected shapes into prefabs to compile them together for easy editing and importing between level projects.

There's also a robust graph-based timeline system that lets you synchronize the actions of nearly any behavior or modifier. You can have multiple timelines as well, which allow you to make actions as varied, detailed, and precise as you want. I've been able to create many types of dynamic platforms, animated NPCs, and background effects with this incredibly useful feature.

Speaking of effects, the sound effect editor is very interesting. Upon generating a sound object, you can choose between a few preset noises as well as form completely new sounds, all from within the editor. There are plenty of audio sliders to toy with as you form the perfect sound effects to compliment the features of your levels. You can also upload a music track to play in the background of your level (provided you have the proper copyrights in order!), which can really help set the mood and atmosphere. I highly recommend experimenting with sounds from time to time, as they can really boost a level's quality.

This only scratches the surface of what the editor can do and, if you ever get stuck while building, the community is more than happy to give you tips and tricks!

[h1]Graphics:[/h1]
Park Bound's core artstyle is a sharp, polygonal look. Your custom character, power-ups, and a few other hardcoded assets follow this style. This is as far as the artstyle goes, however. What do I mean? Well, one misconception about the game is that everything absolutely has to look this way. However, since all of the levels are user-created, anyone is free to push the limits of the engine to their heart's content. Also, if your system has the recommended specs, most levels should run at a smooth 60fps.

[h1]Music/Sound:[/h1]
The game leans towards a catchy 8-bit feel with its default music and sounds. However, since music can be uploaded and most sounds can be altered for each level, most of what you listen to will be a mixed bag of styles. Some players use the default music (which consequently may increase the amount of time you're listening to the same tunes) but there's a shortcut key to mute all music if you need a break or want to listen to something else in the background while you play.

[h1]Community:[/h1]
The community for the game is quite small at the moment (I've been the only player online on quite a few occasions), but most of the current playerbase is very friendly. Most of the players I interact with are very encouraging and give valuable feedback as well. Don't be afraid to ask someone for advice on your next level or chat with them about fun levels you visited! And since users are always creating new areas, there plenty of places to simply hang out as well if you prefer a more laid-back experience.

[h1]Conclusion:[/h1]
If you like creating and sharing levels, you'll almost certainly love this game. If you like platformers, there's an increasing number of 3D levels to try, all with various difficulties. If you like online communities, consider joining us and expanding the player base. If you still aren't sold, I suggest keeping this game on your radar. As time goes on, players join, updates release, and content increases, I'm sure you'll find something to enjoy.

Thank you for reading!
